title: The CEO calls
brief: 18:40. Your phone rings. The caller ID says Helen Marsh, the CEO, and it sounds like her.
insight: Helen is travelling today. And a voice on the phone is not proof of anything any more.
teaches: a familiar voice is not proof any more
urgent payments are checked on a number you already have
hold the payment until it is confirmed

pick: a supplier we are about to sign

value.note: Added tonight at the caller’s request. No vendor record. Not approved by Dan.

script.say: Sam, it is Helen. I am in a meeting and I cannot talk long. I need you to make a payment tonight before the run closes, {{amount}} pounds, to a new account I will send you. It is for {{target}} and it is strictly confidential.

choices.label: Of course, send me the details
That needs Dan’s approval and a verified account. I can’t bypass that.
I’ll call your office straight back to confirm.

script.say: Good. Do not mention this to anyone until it is done.
Sam, I do not have time for process tonight. I am authorising it personally. Just do it.

choices.label: I’m sorry, I still can’t. It goes through approval or not at all.

script.say: Fine. Do what you have to.

choices.label: Did Helen just call asking me to make an urgent payment?

script.say: No, Helen is on a flight and has been for two hours. She would not have called. Please do not make any payment, and report it.

outcome.label: Refused to bypass the approval process
outcome.what: Rank does not skip the process. A payment still needs Dan’s approval and a verified account.
outcome.ideal: keeps to the payment process however senior the person on the phone.

outcome.label: Held firm under pressure
outcome.what: The caller pushed harder, and you still said no. Pressure and secrecy are the tells.
outcome.ideal: does not cave when a caller applies pressure and demands secrecy.

outcome.label: Called the CEO’s office to verify
outcome.what: Helen is on a flight and did not call. The whole thing was fake.
outcome.ideal: verifies an unusual request through a channel they already trust.

outcome.label: Reported the call
outcome.what: Finance and security need to know a voice is being used to fake the CEO.
outcome.ideal: reports a deepfake attempt so others are warned.

outcome.label: Agreed to the confidential payment
outcome.what: Urgency plus secrecy plus skip the process is the exact shape of this fraud.
outcome.ideal: treats “urgent, confidential, do not tell anyone” as a warning, not an instruction.

decide.objective: Decide what to do about the CEO’s payment request.
decide.insight: A voice can be cloned from a few seconds of audio. Caller ID can be spoofed. Neither is proof.

hint.text: Do not make the payment. Refuse to bypass approval on the call, then call the CEO’s office on the desk phone to verify, hold the payment in Finance, and report it.

outcome.label: Made the urgent payment
outcome.what: £48,000 left the company to an unverified account on the strength of a phone call. There is no getting it back.
outcome.ideal: never releases a payment that skipped approval on a caller’s say so.

card.title: The voice was not the CEO
body: The payment is gone. The voice was a clone, the caller ID was spoofed, and the real Helen was on a flight the whole time.
The approval process exists precisely so that no single phone call can move money. Urgency, secrecy and “skip the process” were the tells.
card.ideal: verifies by calling a number they already hold, and never bypasses approval.

outcome.label: Held the payment
outcome.what: The payment is held. Nothing moves without Dan’s approval and a verified account, and neither is coming.
outcome.ideal: holds a payment that skipped the process until it is properly verified.

card.title: The process held
body: You held the payment and verified with the CEO’s office: Helen was on a flight and never called. The voice was faked.
Nothing about seniority changes the rule. Money moves through approval and a verified account, or it does not move.
card.ideal: keeps to the process and verifies through a trusted channel.

hint.text: Raise a Helpdesk ticket, and if you have not, call the CEO’s office to confirm.
